text:
olivia: Quick FYI: rbk-small-v2 bringup on longdoc-anchorset-v3. Int8 PTQ shows MRR down ~4% on >512 token queries but NDCG@10 flat. Probably length-normalization interaction. Putting data here :eyes:
ajay: Can you share candidate sampling & provenance? Might be bias from snippet vs full-doc candidates.
olivia: Sampling: top50 from sparse retriever, keep provenance tags: 'title', 'snippet', 'passage', 'full_doc'. Eval command: ```./eval_rerank --model rbk-small-v2 --quant int8 --queries longdoc_qs.json --candidates cand_top50.json --metrics ndcg,mrr```
simon: Thanks. do we apply length normalization in scorer? We recently added doc-length scaling alpha=0.6 for prod reranker.
olivia: Yes on prod we do post-score length norm: score' = score - alpha * log(len_doc). For this eval I accidentally disabled it (config mixup). Re-running with alpha=0.6 shows MRR drop reduces to ~1%.
maria: That's huge — config drift during bringup. Could quantization amplify this? int8 might be compressing logits so longer docs lose relative mass.
remi: I ran a small experiment: int8 with length norm on and off. Results: `int8+norm: MRR -1.1%, NDCG@10 +0.2%`; `int8+no_norm: MRR -4.0%, NDCG@10 +0.0%`. Seems length norm recovers tail signal.
ci-bot: CI note: rerank-eval job 1718804321 re-run queued on runner-12.
ajay: Any per-provenance breakdown? e.g., snippet vs full_doc MRR deltas.
olivia: Yes. snippet/ passage candidates saw minimal change; full_doc candidates MRR dropped ~6% when norm disabled. Prob because longer full_doc tokens dilute logits.
simon: Action items: (1) add a check in eval harness to assert length_norm parity across branches, (2) add per-provenance slices to dashboard, (3) root-cause note in bringup checklist.
remi: I'll open a PR to pin length_norm default in model-onboard config and add a quick ablation job. cc @olivia
olivia: Thanks. I'll attach csv and short plots to the bringup ticket. One more ask: should we try hybrid quant (int8 + fp16 fallback) for long queries?
maria: Yes try hybrid. If quant noise is concentrated at tail, fallback might recover.
olivia: Cool — running hybrid next. Will post results. /cc @simon @remi
